events.description: US policymakers deliberated about acting against UBL but did not act on the night before the note. The author says this is the third time they balked at 'doing the job'.
The note was sent. It laments policymakers' reluctance to act against UBL and their concern for a mosque, despite four days of bombardment.

US policymakers declined to act on an opportunity to target bin Ladin, which was the third time CIA officers had put him in the government's sights. The author expects they will regret not acting. The date is inferred from 'last night' in a note sent 21 Dec 1998.
Michael Scheuer of CTC sent a note to a recipient whose name is excised (likely Gary Schroen), criticizing policymakers for hesitating over a strike on bin Ladin.

The US bombed Muslim Iraqis for four days (inferred from the garbled 'li-~ql people'). Bin Ladin cited the bombing in his rhetoric, and the author contrasts it with policymakers' worry about the mosque.

relationships.detail: CIA officers repeatedly put UBL in the government's sights for a possible strike, but policymakers did not act.

relationships.detail: Policymakers worried that stray shrapnel from a strike on bin Ladin might hit the Habash mosque, which contributed to the decision not to act. The mosque's link to the target is inferred.

relationships.detail: The deliberations on whether to act against bin Ladin are described as taking place at Langley, CIA headquarters.

key_claims: By 21 December 1998 CIA officers had, on three occasions, put UBL in US government sights, but policymakers backed away each time.
Policymakers worried about collateral damage to a mosque, while the same government had just spent four days bombarding what bin Ladin calls the 'Muslim ... people'.
The author suggests policymakers wanted others to do what the US government would not do, but the relevant OCR text is garbled.
